places.what: STEP and MACULA at every word of our text

record.rule: A reading stands at a word only where a source puts it there by that source's own address, or by a bridge a source declares. Our text and STEP's text (and MACULA's) are two editions of the same verses: a word of ours meets a row of theirs by its place in the verse, never by its letters alone, and the record names how they meet (one for one; one word for two; two for one; the same letters or the letters by which the spelling differs; a verse numbered otherwise; a word written one way and read another, each form with the reading the source gives for it; another word; no row). A source's cells are held whole, byte for byte; nothing is cut, joined, hidden or respelled.
